skill.name: frontend-mobile-security-xss-scan
skill.description: Reviews React, Vue, Angular, and vanilla JavaScript for common XSS sinks, unsafe HTML rendering, URL injection, and missing sanitization.
skill.summary: Finds frontend XSS patterns and suggests framework-aware remediation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All 24 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, TypeScript template literals, documented security commands, and expected local file reads. A separate medium-severity logic flaw can suppress valid React findings when any sanitization term appears elsewhere in a file.

remediation.issue: The React scanner treats any file-wide DOMPurify or sanitize reference as proof that every unsafe HTML sink is protected.
remediation.suggestion: Trace each rendered value to its sink and verify that the exact value passes through an approved sanitizer immediately before rendering.

semantic_findings.title: File-wide sanitization check can hide unsafe React sinks
semantic_findings.description: The React detector suppresses every matching sink when the file contains DOMPurify or sanitize anywhere, even when the vulnerable value never passes through that sanitizer.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The detector passes the complete file to hasSanitization, which returns true from a simple file-wide substring test. This directly creates false negatives.

content.user_title: Scan Frontend Code for XSS Risks
content.value_statement: Unsafe client-side rendering can expose users to script injection. This skill reviews common frontend sinks and provides prioritized remediation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Identifies innerHTML usage associated with common user-input indicators.
Flags React unsafe HTML rendering when sanitization is not detected.
Detects Vue v-html usage and recommends safer rendering options.
Reviews URL assignments for common input indicators and unsafe protocols.
Organizes findings by severity with file locations and remediation guidance.
limitations: The included scanner code is illustrative and omits helper implementations and imports.
String matching does not provide complete source-to-sink data-flow analysis.
File-wide sanitization checks can miss unsafe values that bypass the sanitizer.
The guidance does not cover native iOS or Android rendering APIs.

use_cases.title: Review a feature before merge
use_cases.description: Check changed frontend components for unsafe HTML, URL assignments, and missing sanitization before code review.

use_cases.title: Triage an XSS assessment
use_cases.description: Create an initial list of likely client-side injection sinks for manual verification and prioritization.

use_cases.title: Define secure rendering standards
use_cases.description: Build a framework-specific checklist for React, Vue, Angular, and browser DOM code.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend snippet for XSS risks. Identify unsafe sinks, explain each risk, and suggest a secure alternative: [paste snippet]

prompt_templates.title: Review a framework component
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this [React, Vue, or Angular] component for unsafe HTML rendering, URL injection, and sanitizer misuse: [paste component]
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs framework-specific findings and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Triage repository findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the frontend files in [path]. Prioritize exploitable XSS paths, list evidence, and separate confirmed issues from items needing manual validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A security reviewer needs a prioritized repository assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Perform advanced source-to-sink analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace untrusted data from [sources] to HTML, script, URL, and event-handler sinks. Evaluate sanitization by context and document likely false negatives.
prompt_templates.scenario: An experienced reviewer needs deeper data-flow and context analysis.

output_examples.input: Review a React component that renders customer-provided rich text.
output: High: Unsafe HTML rendering accepts customer-controlled content.
Verify that the exact rendered value passes through an allowlist-based HTML sanitizer.
Prefer plain-text rendering when rich HTML is not required.

output_examples.input: Check a navigation helper that assigns a query parameter to the browser location.
output: High: User-controlled URL data reaches a navigation sink.
Allow only expected HTTP or HTTPS destinations.
Reject script and data protocols before assignment.

best_practices: Provide complete files or relevant data-flow context around each suspected sink.
Verify every reported path manually before treating it as exploitable.
Run framework tests and browser security tests after applying remediation.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a sanitizer import proves that every rendered value is sanitized.
Do not classify every innerHTML occurrence as exploitable without tracing its input.
Do not replace contextual validation with simple keyword matching.

faq.question: Which frameworks does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It provides patterns for React, Vue, Angular, and vanilla browser JavaScript.

faq.question: Does it modify application code?
faq.answer: No. It reviews code and proposes remediation unless the user separately requests edits.

faq.question: Can it prove that an XSS issue is exploitable?
faq.answer: No. Findings require manual data-flow review and environment-specific validation.

faq.question: Does it support native mobile applications?
faq.answer: No. The documented checks target web frontend code, not native iOS or Android APIs.

faq.question: Does it require external tools?
faq.answer: Core guidance does not. Optional examples reference ESLint, Semgrep, DOMPurify, and a custom Node.js scanner.

faq.question: How should sanitization findings be reviewed?
faq.answer: Confirm that the exact untrusted value uses a context-appropriate sanitizer immediately before reaching the sink.
